facts.fact: Connecting Africa reports that Safaricom Ethiopia was given a Payment Instrument Issuer licence by the National Bank of Ethiopia, three months before M-Pesa went live in August 2023.

KEN.note: No Kenyan central bank role is stated.

facts.fact: Connecting Africa reports Safaricom extended M-Pesa Global to Ethiopia in October 2024, so M-Pesa wallets in Kenya and Ethiopia can make cross-border transfers, with Ethiopian customers receiving from M-Pesa Kenya.

Connecting Africa reports Safaricom extended M-Pesa Global to Ethiopia in October 2024, so M-Pesa wallets in Kenya and Ethiopia can make cross-border transfers, and M-Pesa customers can send and receive in over 190 countries.

ETH.note: No government payments to people are mentioned.

KEN.note: No government payments to people are mentioned.

ETH.note: The 4.5 million registered M-Pesa users is a provider count, not a survey.

KEN.note: No account ownership survey is mentioned.

facts.fact: Connecting Africa reports M-Pesa went live in Ethiopia in August 2023, with 4.5 million registered mobile money users by May 2024.

KEN.note: Kenyan M-Pesa is named only as the sending end of the corridor.

ETH.note: No tax or fee payment is mentioned.
